text:
alex: Hey all — first day! 😅 On a Macbook Air M2. Trying to get dev env up: asdf for node/ruby, Homebrew, dotfiles symlinked to ~/dotfiles. asdf shims don't seem to be taking effect and `node --version` gives system node. Anyone have the quick checklist for mac (zsh) so I don't break things? Also I couldn't find REDWOOD_API_KEY instructions — is that in 1Password or envrc?
rebecca: welcome alex :tada: quick checklist: 1) ensure Homebrew is the arm64 path (/opt/homebrew) 2) add asdf init to your shell rc 3) source your dotfiles installer. Try:```
# add to ~/.zprofile (for zsh login shells)
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
eval "$(asdf shell init zsh)"
```
rebecca: if you used homebrew from intel (/usr/local) you'll get path conflicts — run `brew --prefix` to confirm.
toni: also double-check ~/.tool-versions in repo root or your $HOME. asdf reads in that order. if you're seeing system node, run `asdf reshim nodejs` after installing the plugin and version.
alex: thanks! I did `asdf install` but forgot `reshim`. running that now. for REDWOOD_API_KEY where should I pull it from? I see a vault entry but not sure which one.
marta: we keep service creds in 1Password > Redwood > Dev Keys. Ask Camila or PM if you need a new key. For local dev you can use a personal test key with limited scope — open a ticket in #support and we'll provision if needed.
ash: (bot message) Welcome message: Hi alex! If you need machine setup help, book a 30m pairing session with eng-devex: https://cal.com/redwood/devex — reply "book" here and the bot will DM you.
ash: FYI we prefer storing ephemeral local env vars with direnv/envrc; if you use that, add REDWOOD_API_KEY to .envrc and `direnv allow`.
ash: (continuing) If you're on mac and using Zsh, prefer ~/.zprofile for PATHs and ~/.zshrc for interactive aliases.
alex: ran reshim — node now shows v20.6.1. thanks! dotfiles installer errored on gpg key import (pinentry). any tips?
ash: for gpg on mac, install pinentry-mac via brew and set `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in your shell. also run `gpg --card-status` if using yubikey.
ash: if pinentry still prompts in GUI, try `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent` then `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`.
ash: if you want, I can drop a short checklist to the repo README for new-hires.
rebecca: also note: if you use brew-installed openssl for ruby builds, set:```export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"
``` and then reinstall ruby via asdf plugin.
ash: one last thing — if you hit docker permission errors, run `sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) /var/run/docker.sock` (or use our devcontainer).
alex: awesome, everything green except gpg pinentry. I'll try the pinentry-mac fix and ping if still stuck. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
